title: Evolve Rust string-utils library in 3 steps: reverse, palindrome, truncate
description: The rust_string_utils library has word_count and capitalize_words. Evolve it in three steps by adding reverse_words, is_palindrome_phrase, and truncate.

task_spec.prompt:
The library in src/lib.rs has word_count and capitalize_words. Evolve it in three steps:

Step 1 — reverse_words:
  pub fn reverse_words(s: &str) -> String
  Returns the words of s in reversed order, joined by a single space.
  'hello world foo' -> 'foo world hello'
  Empty string or all-whitespace -> ''
  Add test_reverse_words_basic and test_reverse_words_empty.

Step 2 — is_palindrome_phrase:
  pub fn is_palindrome_phrase(s: &str) -> bool
  Returns true if the phrase reads the same forwards and backwards when lowercased and all non-alphabetic characters removed.
  'A man a plan a canal Panama' -> true
  'hello world' -> false
  Add test_palindrome_true and test_palindrome_false.

Step 3 — truncate:
  pub fn truncate(s: &str, max_len: usize, suffix: &str) -> String
  If s.len() <= max_len, return s unchanged.
  Otherwise return &s[..max_len] + suffix.
  Slicing is by characters (use char_indices), not bytes.
  Add test_truncate_short (no change), test_truncate_long (appends suffix), test_truncate_unicode (handles multibyte).

All 3 existing tests must still pass.

Run cargo test to confirm.
required_artifacts: pub fn truncate(s: &str, max_len: usize, suffix: &str) -> String added
success_criteria: is_palindrome_phrase ignores case and non-alpha chars
truncate uses char boundaries not byte boundaries
